messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call (incidents). High-priority alert: possible cross-tenant KV access detected originating from Dedicated pool gp-dedicated-3. Affected tenant: zenith. Automatic isolation rule triggered? yes. Please acknowledge and triage — runbook: https://playbooks.redwood/tenant-isolation
oncall-aaron: ack. I'm on it. Initial artifact: noticed `kv_get` returned keys with prefix `zenith/` while request context tenant_id=zenith-prod, but client IP maps to pod from pool gp-dedicated-3 that currently hosts both zenith and other customers per allocation table.
oncall-aaron: grabbing logs. running quick query against audit stream: `select * from kv_access where key like 'zenith/%' and pool='gp-dedicated-3' limit 50`
platform-eng-lucas: adding context — we had a routing change 23m ago to rebind pool gp-dedicated-3 to the new edge-eu router, rollback happened partially. Could be stale route table entry that left an old mapping between namespace->pool. I'm checking infra diff.
infra-nora: saw an automated deploy to pool mapping service at 2026-03-15T09:07:12Z. The rollout created a gradual change with a 5% backoff stage. Canary logs show mapping update for tenant `zenith` to route-id `r-eu-17`.
oncall-aaron: timeline: alert fired at 1979971234 (root), deployment at 1979971000 (~3.9m earlier). The KV access anomalies spike at +120s after the deployment.
customer-ops-zenith: we are seeing customer errors — they reported data they shouldn't have access to. Please keep us updated, this is impacting a production customer.
security-sam: this is critical from a compliance POV. Collect evidence steps: snapshot audit logs, preserve KV shards, capture in-flight requests. Also disable cross-tenant read paths ASAP.
oncall-aaron: step 1: isolating tenant by moving zenith to a new dedicated allocation and removing shared mounts from gp-dedicated-3. Command: `ri pool-assign --tenant zenith --pool gp-zenith-temp --evict-shared` — running now.
platform-eng-lucas: suggestion — instead of evicting which can take time, we can apply an ACL rule at the pool-proxy level to drop reads for keys matching `zenith/*` from non-zenith contexts. Pushing ACL rule now: 
```
proxyctl patch-acl --pool gp-dedicated-3 --add "deny read if request.tenant != 'zenith' and key.startsWith('zenith/')"
```
oncall-aaron: ACL applied, confirm probes.
infra-nora: probe results: 200/200 writes work for zenith. 403s returned for cross-tenant read attempts. Audit stream showing `deny` events: 17 so far. Good immediate mitigation.
oncall-aaron: still seeing some anomalous reads (3 requests) that bypassed proxy and hit shard directly — likely due to cached endpoint IP on client side. Security: can we revoke stale certificates for pool nodes to break those connections?
security-sam: yes. revoking TLS certs for affected nodes forces reconnect. Plan: `certctl revoke --node nodexx` for nodes in gp-dedicated-3. Doing in rolling fashion to avoid mass disruption.
oncall-aaron: started cert revoke for nodes [gp3-n1,gp3-n2]. Noting potential brief client reconnects. Notifying customer.
customer-ops-zenith: appreciate the updates. We need a timeline for impacted queries and confirmation that no PII was exposed.
oncall-aaron: collecting list of returned keys and sample payloads. PII scan in progress: `pii-scan --input audit_dump.json --patterns ssn,email,phone`
platform-eng-lucas: found the root cause: a race in pool-mapper service when a partial rollback left obsolete binding `namespace_prefix -> pool` entries for tenants that previously had ephemeral multiplexing. For zenith the prefix `zenith/` was erroneously associated with gp-dedicated-3 in the ephemeral cache even though allocation moved. Fix: hotpatch pool-mapper to invalidate caches on rollback and enforce strict non-overlap on prefix claims.
oncall-aaron: hotpatch applied to pool-mapper (commit `a3f9c2`). Will monitor metrics.
infra-nora: eviction to gp-zenith-temp completed. Replication sync verified. Confirming no more direct-shard hits from non-zenith contexts.
oncall-aaron: running end-to-end canary: 
```
# canary script
curl -H "x-tenant: zenith" https://api.redwood/v1/kv/zenith/foo -> 200
curl -H "x-tenant: other" https://api.redwood/v1/kv/zenith/foo -> 403
```
sre-lead-maya: taking over. Thanks @oncall-aaron for triage. Actions for next 24h: 1) forensic export and secure storage of audit logs, 2) postmortem with timeline and RCA, 3) platform change to pool-mapper + stricter pre-deploy checks, 4) customer communication draft and compensation review. I'll schedule a follow-up bridge in 30m.
security-sam: confirm we have snapshots of raw KV shards and the writes history. I've kicked off a snapshot job and written to secure object storage with restricted ACLs.
customer-ops-zenith: any ETA on full revert of shared allocations? We need assurance of full tenancy separation.
sre-lead-maya: we've completed tenant eviction and proxy ACLs. Full root cause fix will be deployed in the next maintenance window unless we approve hotfix (recommended). I'll coordinate with product and ops.
oncall-aaron: closing the immediate page. Monitoring for 30m. If anything, re-page SRE. Copying evidence to `#incidents-evidence/1979971234`
pagerbot: Incident update: mitigation applied (proxy ACL + cert revocation + eviction). Severity reduced to P2. Please attach all artifacts to the ticket: INC-2026-6789.
sre-lead-maya: handover notes: primary mitigations done. Next: rollback-proofing, deploy-time invariants, add unit test in pool-mapper to catch stale-cache scenarios. Assigning follow-ups to platform-eng-lucas and infra-nora.
platform-eng-lucas: acknowledged. Will open PR with cache invalidation tests and add a CI gate.
customer-ops-zenith: thanks. Please share final incident report and confirm whether any customer data left the environment.
sre-lead-maya: we'll include full evidence in the postmortem. Preliminary scan shows only metadata fragments, no clear PII exfil. Security will confirm after deep scan. Closing thread once evidence uploaded.
